messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: RT-P99-LATENCY fired for service=canary-worker (env=prod-canary). Triggered by 5/5 synthetic checks failing within 30s. incident_id=INC7843219000

maria: acked. I'm on it. seeing the same spike on the canary dashboard. no user-facing SLO breach yet.

aman: thanks. can you grab the canary logs? i want to check if this is autoscaler churn or something upstream.

maria: pulling logs now. quick grep shows repeated OOMs on the worker pods then restarts. snippet: ```
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z canary-worker-7bdf crash: OOMKilled memory=11.9Gi 
2026-03-15T10:12:04Z canary-worker-7bdf kubelet: restarting container
```

lee: hmm autoscaler recently reduced per-pod memory limit in the recent scheduler tweak, could be related. which revision is this canary pinned to?

maria: canary -> model-serving:v2.3.2, config shows mem_limit=12Gi (weird, those OOMs are right at the boundary).

incident-bot: escalation: no escalation required (ack by maria). auto-resolve window set to 5m.

aman: if it's OOM, we can either bump limit or temporarily scale up replica count to spread load. but it's a canary group — prefer to fail fast. suggestion: silence pagerduty for the canary checks while we triage so we don't flood pages. PD silence id pending.

maria: creating PD silence now for rule:prod-canary-monitor, duration=10m. ```pd-cli silence create --rule prod-canary-monitor --duration 10m --reason "triage OOM"``` 

pd-bot: PagerDuty silence created (silence_id=SIL7843219000) by maria; will expire in 10m.

lee: good. while silenced can we re-deploy canary with mem_limit=14Gi to validate quickly? if the latest scheduler change is too aggressive we need to revert.

maria: deploying quick patch: set mem_limit=14Gi and restart canary pods. ```kubectl -n prod-canary set resources deployment/canary-worker --limits=memory=14Gi```

aman: i'll watch the canary dashboard and traces. maria, let us know if the synthetic checks start passing.

maria: restart started. new pods coming up. initial metrics: p95 latency back to baseline, no OOMs in last 30s.

incident-bot: alert auto-resolve: RT-P99-LATENCY for prod-canary resolved (auto-resolve by monitoring) at 2026-03-15T10:13:10Z.

maria: can confirm canary synthetic checks returned green. removing PD silence early. pd-cli silence remove SIL7843219000.

pd-bot: PagerDuty silence SIL7843219000 removed by maria.

lee: thanks all. quick root-cause hypothesis: scheduler memory limit change + tight canary memory equals OOM churn causing spike in synthetic latency.

aman: agree. action items: 1) revert or adjust scheduler change (lee + infra) 2) add debounce in incident-bot for canary group to require 2 consecutive failures in 60s before paging (maria + devex) 3) add canary pod mem headroom to config (product + eng-runtime) 4) post-incident note in #incidents (maria).

maria: taking action items 2 and 4. will open a tiny RFC for canary debounce and a follow-up postmortem.

lee: i'll coordinate with infra to roll back the scheduler tweak and propose safer defaults.

aman: i'm going to scan other canary clusters for similar OOM boundary issues. will report back in the postmortem doc.

maria: handing off to lee for overnight watch. leaving notes in ops-runbook. @lee you're the follow-up oncall, check the runbook if anything fires overnight. :point_right:

lee: got it, taking handoff. i'll post summary in #incidents in 30m with links.

incident-bot: handoff recorded: from=maria to=lee at 2026-03-15T10:14:50Z.

maria: thanks team :thumbsup: keeping this thread open for any late regressions.

lee: ping me if you see any re-occurrence. otherwise i'll close the loop after postmortem doc is up.

aman: small note — add a metric alert for OOMKill rate on canary nodes; that'll help catch this pattern earlier.

maria: noted. adding to action items.

pd-bot: Incident INC7843219000 marked as resolved in PagerDuty.

maria: closing thread from oncall perspective, will update when postmortem RFC is ready.

lee: closing as followup in morning. night all.
